extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry / commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_short: criteria for flatness in algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted collection of theorems, exercises, and useful tests from a textbook section about flatness of modules and morphisms: includes local, infinitesimal, valuative, slicing, fibral, generic, and cohomological criteria and consequences. Intended as checks one can perform to decide or use flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphism / rank criterion for local freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is finite, and Y is reduced and locally Noetherian. Then O_X is locally free iff the rank of π_* O_X (i.e., dim_{κ(q)} (π_* O_X ⊗ κ(q))) is a locally constant function of q in Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a simple test for when a finite map is flat (finite + locally free = finite flat). See hint referencing Exercise 13.7.K and surrounding discussion; reducedness and local Noetherian hypotheses are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for flatness over a regular curve (associated-points test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a morphism from a locally Noetherian scheme X to a regular (locally Noetherian) curve Y. Then π is flat iff all associated points of X map to the generic point of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a geometric, easy-to-visualize criterion for flatness in one-parameter families (partial converse to the fact that flat maps send associated points to associated points). It generalizes immediately to coherent sheaves on X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for flatness (DVR test)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finitely presented morphism π: X → Y, if for every morphism Y' → Y with Y' = Spec of a discrete valuation ring the base-change X ×_Y Y' has no associated points mapping to the closed point of Y', then (under reduced + locally Noetherian hypotheses on Y) π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If π is flat then this property holds for each DVR test; conversely, reduced + locally Noetherian base makes it sufficient. This is called a valuative criterion for flatness and provides an intuitive way to visualize flatness via behavior over DVRs. (See reference to Gr–EGA IV.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of flat closures / flat limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A a DVR, X a locally Noetherian A-scheme, and Y a closed subscheme of the generic fiber X_η, there is a unique closed subscheme Y' of X with Y'|_η = Y and Y' flat over A; Y'|_0 is the flat limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to define and compute flat limits in one-parameter degenerations. Exercises (24.4.K, 24.4.L, 24.4.N, etc.) show how to compute explicit flat limits and check nonreduced structure; uniqueness is part of the criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful flatness: definitions and equivalent tests
rubrics_metrics.description: A B-module M is faithfully flat if M is flat and for all B-modules N, M ⊗_B N = 0 implies N = 0; equivalently M ⊗_B κ(p) ≠ 0 for every prime p of B (or for every maximal ideal m). For a morphism π: X → Y, faithful flatness means flat and surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faithful flatness can be tested by checking non-vanishing of fibers at primes/maximals. Faithful flatness is preserved by base change and composition, and useful for deducing geometric consequences such as openness, going-down, etc. See Exercises 24.5.A–D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-Down Theorem for flat morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is flat over B (ring morphism), then given primes q' ⊂ q in B and a prime p' in A lying above q', there exists a prime p ⊂ A with p' ⊂ p mapping to q. Equivalently, flat morphisms satisfy a Going-Down property for primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key topological consequence of flatness (useful in dimension arguments). The exercise suggests reducing to localizations to show faithful flatness and then apply going-down; see Exercises 24.5.E and related remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat morphisms (locally finite type, Noetherian) are open maps
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is locally of finite type and flat with Y (hence X) locally Noetherian, then π is an open map (sends open sets to open sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: reduce to affine case, show image is constructible (Chevalley), then use Going-Down for flat morphisms to show closure under generization, and conclude openness. See Exercise 24.5.G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension behavior for flat morphisms (fiber dimension additivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and p ∈ X with q = π(p), codim_X p = codim_Y q + codim_{π^{-1}(q)} p. Informally: locally, dim fiber = dim X − dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives precise control of fiber dimensions in flat families (no unexpected jumps in fiber dimension when flat). Use Going-Down and chain-building arguments (Exercise 24.5.H) to prove the reverse inequality and obtain equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat of relative dimension n
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y is 'flat of relative dimension n' if π is flat, locally of finite type, and all fibers have pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The locally finite type hypothesis ensures reasonable behavior (e.g., preservation under base change). See surrounding discussion (24.5.7–24.5.9) for caveats and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic flatness (existence of dense open of flatness)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite type with Y Noetherian integral and F a coherent sheaf on X, then there exists a dense open U ⊂ Y such that F is flat over U (i.e., flat at all points mapping to U). In particular, for O_X this gives generic flatness of morphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a consequence of Grothendieck's Generic Freeness Lemma (Exercise 24.5.M). An improved form (Theorem 24.5.12 / Stacks tag 052B) gives finite presentation + flatness on a dense open when Y is reduced and F finite type coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness is an open condition (flat locus is open)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y locally finite type morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and F a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf on X: (a) the locus in X where F is Y-flat is open; (b) if π is closed (e.g., proper), then the locus in Y over which F is flat is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from generic flatness and deeper commutative algebra results (cited references: Matsumura, EGA, Stacks). Use Noetherian or local finite presentation hypotheses as appropriate (Theorem 24.5.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local criterion for flatness (Noetherian local ring, Tor test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 24.6.1: If (A,m) is a Noetherian local ring and M a finitely generated A-module, then M is flat iff Tor^A_1(M, A/m) = 0. More generally (24.6.2), for a local morphism (B,n) → (A,m) and M a finitely generated A-module, M is B-flat iff Tor^B_1(M, B/n) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a powerful and commonly used test reducing flatness to a single Tor-vanishing calculation at the closed point; finite generation hypotheses are essential. The proof uses Artin–Rees / Krull intersection arguments (see Theorem 24.6.2 & proof sketch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinitesimal criterion for flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: If (B,n) → (A,m) is a local homomorphism and M a finitely generated A-module such that for each t ≥ 0 the quotient M / n^t M is flat over B / n^t, then M is flat over B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows flatness can be tested on all infinitesimal thickenings; combined with other lemmas it yields alternative proofs of the local criterion. See Exercise 24.6.C and the proof structure of Theorem 24.6.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion for flatness (nonzerodivisor test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (B,n) → (A,m) be a local morphism of Noetherian local rings, M a finitely generated A-module, and t ∈ B a nonzerodivisor contained in n. Then M is B-flat iff (i) t is not a zerodivisor on M, and (ii) M/tM is flat over B/(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a convenient inductive / slicing test: check flatness after cutting by a nonzerodivisor and check t doesn't introduce torsion. Lemma 24.6.6 relates Tor over B to Tor over B/(t) and is used in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local slicing (relative effective Cartier divisors stay flat)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is flat and Z ⊂ X is a relative effective Cartier divisor (locally principal and a Cartier divisor on fibers), then Z is flat over Y (Exercise 24.6.F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation of Exercise 24.6.F: slicing in the source preserves flatness for relative effective Cartier divisors; used in many geometric constructions (e.g., relative divisors in flat families).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibral Flatness Theorem (equivalence of fibral vs total flatness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram X --π--> Z and X --τ--> Y with ρ: Y → Z, for a finitely presented quasi-coherent sheaf F and points p ∈ X, q = π(p) ∈ Z, r = τ(p) ∈ Y with F_p ≠ 0, then (a) F is τ-flat at p and the restriction F|_r is π_r-flat at p iff (b) ρ is flat at q and F is π-flat at p (under Noetherian or finite presentation hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a way to deduce flatness of F over a larger base from flatness over fibers and flatness of the base-change map. See references to EGA / Stacks for proof (24.6.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness implies constant Euler characteristic in projective families
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is projective and locally Noetherian and F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y, then χ(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is a locally constant function of q ∈ Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key cohomological consequence: in flat projective families Euler characteristic of fibers is locally constant. Proof uses Serre vanishing, Cech complexes of flat sheaves, and vanishing of higher pushforwards for large twists (Theorem 24.7.1). This yields necessary conditions for flatness and connects to semicontinuity theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity of cohomology in flat limits (cohomology can only jump up)
rubrics_metrics.description: In flat limits cohomology groups can only jump up: for a flat family the dimensions h^i of cohomology are upper-semicontinuous, and in concrete degenerations one sees h^i increase in the special fiber rather than decrease (example: twisted cubic degenerating to nodal cubic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an informal moral leading to the Semicontinuity Theorem (28.1.1) and is used to reason about behavior of h^0, h^1 in degenerations; also explains constancy of Euler characteristic in flat families.
